name: Verified bounded completion
conditions: Specific operation has current authority, correct subject and meaning, and independently adequate effect evidence.
feedback: None required. Completion is an endpoint for this operation, not an attracting operating regime.
entry: Resolve discrepancies before effect, or reconcile the actual effect with adequate independent evidence.
exit: New contradictory evidence reopens the assessment; new work is a different operation.
survives: Accountable result and usable evidence for the bounded claim.
lost: No guarantee about unrelated operations or future effects.
falsifier: An independently verified mismatch in recipient, units, authority, or effect refutes the completion claim.
evidence: Qualitative conditional hypothesis from assigned scenarios; not observed in Factory.

name: Explicit validity hold
conditions: A functioning gate refuses ambiguous identity, version, freshness, or authority before the next effect.
feedback: No autonomous restoring force. A retained refusal condition keeps work held.
entry: Mismatch is detected while the relevant gate remains in control.
exit: Supply current compatible evidence and legitimate authorization, or abandon work; neither implies past effects were undone.
survives: Inspectability and any unaffected local functions; abstention from this next gated action.
lost: Throughput for held work; possibly its deadline.
falsifier: Effects proceed despite the alleged gate, or an ungated participant still accepts old requests.
evidence: Source supports only local attempt-budget refusal and explicit resume; generic semantic and provider gates are stipulated, not implemented guarantees.

name: Effect unknown and retry withheld
conditions: An attempt may have crossed the boundary; evidence is insufficient and further attempts are withheld.
feedback: None inherent. Missing information plus refusal policy sustains the wait, not attraction.
entry: Lost acknowledgment, ambiguous restoration, or missing participant history.
exit: Correlated participant/recipient evidence resolves outcome; explicit risk acceptance may permit a new attempt without resolving the old one.
survives: Honest uncertainty and remaining local attempt evidence.
lost: Known outcome and automatic progress; old work can still act.
falsifier: Independent evidence proves rejection or acceptance, or a retry loop actually continues.
evidence: Source supports journal-before-writer and restore blocking for retained attempted tasks. It does not prove business-effect reconciliation or recover missing journal suffixes.

name: Settled but semantically wrong result
conditions: Structurally valid data or a reported result has the wrong units, person, context, or interpretation.
feedback: None necessary. One wrong completion does not establish a reinforcing loop.
entry: Semantic check absent or shares the same error; work is marked finished.
exit: Independent domain comparison exposes error; correction is new work and may leave irreversible consequences.
survives: Bytes, signatures, task status, and sometimes technical service availability.
lost: Correct business meaning; apparent success is not evidence of it.
falsifier: Independent subject and quantity verification agrees with the intended operation.
evidence: Source completion validates result presence/size and transition, not artifact truth. Unit, identity and real-world errors remain hypothetical.

name: Self-confirming false record
conditions: Wrong canonical input feeds all verification, backup and future decisions; those decisions promote that input as trusted again.
feedback: Wrong record -> agreeing checks -> confidence and reuse -> replacement of alternatives -> stronger dependence on wrong record. Loop can persist after the original defect stops.
entry: Common exporter/table/decoder plus no independent semantic anchor and repeated reuse.
exit: A genuinely independent anchor contradicts the record and is allowed to change decisions; corrected bytes alone do not restore lost history.
survives: Internally consistent operations and repeatable but wrong outputs.
lost: Independent grounding and, if alternatives overwritten, recoverable original truth.
falsifier: Checks use a different origin and surface the discrepancy, or no decisions feed records back into future trust.
evidence: Qualitative conditional hypothesis from assigned scenarios; not observed in Factory.

name: Confidentiality already lost
conditions: An unauthorized party has actually learned confidential content or identifying metadata.
feedback: No feedback needed. Knowledge cannot be made never learned; further distribution is contingent.
entry: Export, labels, routing responses, or geographic transfer disclose protected information to an unauthorized observer.
exit: No exit from historical disclosure. Containment can stop future access but cannot guarantee forgetting.
survives: Local operations may remain intact; evidence of disclosure may survive.
lost: Prior exclusivity of disclosed knowledge, not automatically all future privacy.
falsifier: No unauthorized party could access or infer the information; protected ciphertext without a key is not disclosure.
evidence: Qualitative conditional hypothesis from assigned scenarios; not observed in Factory.

name: Active probing and response cycle
conditions: An observer repeatedly induces alerts and can correlate their responses with recipients or timing.
feedback: Each response improves the next probe, but continued probes require an active external actor.
entry: Observable timing/routing variation and alert-triggering access.
exit: Probing stops or responses cease to distinguish recipients; learned information remains BD06.
survives: Business services and perhaps alert delivery.
lost: Secrecy of response patterns and attention capacity.
falsifier: Observed responses have no correlation with real recipient availability or identities.
evidence: Qualitative conditional hypothesis from assigned scenarios; not observed in Factory.

name: Competing writers and repairs
conditions: Two writers retain effective mutation authority and each treats the other writer changes as drift requiring repair.
feedback: Writer A changes state -> B repairs toward B view -> A repairs toward A view. No new split-brain event is needed once both loops exist.
entry: Clone or repair kernel receives independent authority without effective shared exclusion.
exit: One authority becomes ineffective at every affected participant, followed by reconciliation of already accepted effects.
survives: Both local histories and plausible liveness may persist.
lost: Single authoritative history and predictable action count.
falsifier: One writer is actually rejected at the participant, or neither writer reacts to the other; then only a finite conflict occurred.
evidence: Qualitative conditional hypothesis from assigned scenarios; not observed in Factory.

name: Delayed work has outlived its authority
conditions: Queued or recovering work remains deliverable after authority, prohibition, identity context or safety conditions change.
feedback: None required. Delay creates a hazardous interval; it ends only with expiry enforcement, rejection, acceptance, or cancellation evidence.
entry: Validation happened earlier than the last boundary that can cause the effect.
exit: Participant refuses stale work -> BD02/BD25; acceptance may yield BD10; no outcome evidence -> BD03.
survives: Historical authorization and operation identity, if retained.
lost: Assurance that past approval still covers present execution.
falsifier: All effect-capable participants enforce current validity at acceptance, not merely at enqueue.
evidence: Qualitative conditional hypothesis from assigned scenarios; not observed in Factory.

name: Past external effect cannot be rolled back
conditions: An effect actually occurred and its relevant dimension is irreversible, such as disclosure, injury, or an unretractable communication.
feedback: None. Absorption is relative to the past event; repairable financial balance is not automatically irreversible harm.
entry: A wrong, duplicated, expired or prohibited action is accepted and has an irreversible consequence.
exit: No restoration of the prior world on that dimension; compensation may improve later conditions.
survives: Whatever records, authority and unaffected resources remain.
lost: Ability to make the past effect not have happened.
falsifier: No effect occurred, or the claimed lost property is fully reversible and no irreversible dimension is shown.
evidence: Qualitative conditional hypothesis from assigned scenarios; not observed in Factory.

name: Writer handoff ownership unknown
conditions: A handoff loses its acknowledgment and neither available evidence nor authority determines who may write.
feedback: None inherent. Choosing abstention preserves the wait; guessing can enter BD08.
entry: Communication breaks between relinquishment, transfer and activation.
exit: Durable ownership evidence from the relevant authority identifies one effective writer, or a legitimate new authority excludes both old contenders.
survives: Local stores and handoff fragments.
lost: Known ownership and safe immediate writes.
falsifier: Atomic local-only migration or a durable ownership register resolves the alleged gap.
evidence: Qualitative conditional hypothesis from assigned scenarios; not observed in Factory.

name: Recovery prerequisite deadlock
conditions: Restoring capability A requires reading or changing B, but B is accessible only through broken A; no independent bootstrap path exists.
feedback: Circular dependency, not a demonstrated attractor: each prerequisite waits for the other.
entry: Optional plugin becomes the exclusive reader of its own emergency configuration, or credential repair itself needs the unavailable credential.
exit: An independent readable configuration, compatible bootstrap binary, or legitimate credential path exists; permanent loss may instead end service.
survives: Raw bytes or unaffected scopes if separately accessible.
lost: In-band repair capability.
falsifier: An offline reader or safe local startup path can operate without the broken prerequisite.
evidence: Qualitative conditional hypothesis from assigned scenarios; not observed in Factory.

name: Maintenance lock-in
conditions: Knowledge/build dependencies are scarce and incidents consume the effort needed to reduce that scarcity.
feedback: Repair difficulty -> ad hoc patch or deferral -> less understood/reproducible system -> greater next repair difficulty. Persists after one maintainer departure if incident effort dominates learning.
entry: Hidden assumptions, vanished toolchain/account, and no effective knowledge transfer or reproducible substitute.
exit: A successor demonstrates independent rebuild and operation, or service is retired; a funding injection alone does not prove exit.
survives: Existing binary may keep working and source may remain readable.
lost: Confident change capability and timely repairs.
falsifier: A new maintainer can reproduce and repair using documented local inputs; one missing person alone creates no loop.
evidence: Qualitative conditional hypothesis from assigned scenarios; not observed in Factory.

name: Exception-driven authority erosion
conditions: Exceptions allowing effects become precedents and incidents are handled by adding more exceptions rather than resolving their meaning.
feedback: Ambiguous exception -> discretionary bypass -> precedent and extra branch -> greater ambiguity. Installed policy and incentives sustain the loop.
entry: Accumulated special cases with no comprehensible authority ordering.
exit: Decision-makers can explain and consistently apply effective authority for counterexamples, or operations stop pending authority resolution.
survives: Ability to perform work and a nominal approval vocabulary.
lost: Predictable authorization meaning and trustworthy audit interpretation.
falsifier: All sampled conflicting cases resolve under one understood rule without adding a bypass.
evidence: Qualitative conditional hypothesis from assigned scenarios; not observed in Factory.

name: Common dependency outage
conditions: Different nominal services share a cloud, billing, credential or mandatory startup dependency that is unavailable.
feedback: No internal feedback required; the unavailable common prerequisite sustains the outage. Retry feedback belongs to BD24 separately.
entry: Shared infrastructure fails, payment is suspended, or optional monitoring becomes a mandatory root dependency.
exit: Prerequisite recovers or operations genuinely become independent of it; permanent supplier loss can enter BD22.
survives: Offline records and local functions only if not startup-gated by that dependency.
lost: Correlated service, backup and alert availability, not automatically existing backup bytes.
falsifier: A claimed independent component continues operating through a real failure of the shared prerequisite.
evidence: Qualitative conditional hypothesis from assigned scenarios; not observed in Factory.

name: Test evidence cannot see the defect
conditions: Fixtures, clocks or mocks exclude delayed acceptance, real fencing behavior or shared timing failure.
feedback: No production loop inferred. Passing tests can reinforce confidence, but operational behavior is unspecified.
entry: Test oracle shares the assumption being tested or time never advances independently.
exit: A discriminating trace from a separately controlled boundary reveals whether the omitted behavior matters.
survives: Evidence for the cases actually represented by tests.
lost: Justification for extrapolating test success to omitted failures.
falsifier: The suite independently represents and rejects the omitted interleaving or provider behavior.
evidence: Source adapter tests use FakeHerdr and recorded payloads; this does not establish that every repository test has these blind spots. Scenario-specific omissions are stipulated.

name: Signal present but not actionable by the human
conditions: An alert exists but the intended human cannot perceive, receive or uniquely interpret it, and no other effective responder acts.
feedback: No intrinsic loop; access, language, display or channel conditions maintain the gap.
entry: Color-only warning, truncated identity, misleading translation, or powered-off phone.
exit: An accessible unambiguous observation reaches a legitimate responder; action still needs correct authority and repair capacity.
survives: Possibly working monitor and local diagnostic evidence.
lost: Timely human understanding; detection is not intervention.
falsifier: The actual operator identifies the right state and instance without relying on the ambiguous channel.
evidence: Qualitative conditional hypothesis from assigned scenarios; not observed in Factory.

name: Alert workload sustains non-response
conditions: Outstanding alerts/escalations consume more attention than responders can clear, and unresolved incidents produce further reminders or faults.
feedback: Backlog -> less repair time -> unresolved faults/reminders -> more backlog. Can persist after flapping stops only if this endogenous production exceeds clearance.
entry: Large alarm burst or costly false positives with inadequate effective attention capacity.
exit: Net endogenous alert production falls below clearance and actual faults are repaired; muting alone may instead enter BD21 or BD19.
survives: Raw alerts and some service functions.
lost: Signal salience and timely diagnosis.
falsifier: After the initial burst ends, backlog drains without recurring production; then it was a finite transient, not this attractor.
evidence: Qualitative conditional hypothesis from assigned scenarios; not observed in Factory.

name: Acknowledged but deliberately deferred
conditions: Acknowledgment closes the paging obligation but does not allocate timely repair, and the queue permits indefinite deferral.
feedback: No autonomous feedback required; scheduling policy retains the backlog. Repeated deferral may participate in BD18.
entry: A human acknowledges and queues repair far beyond acceptable time.
exit: Repair is actually executed and its outcome checked, or the work is explicitly abandoned.
survives: Ownership/acknowledgment evidence and potentially diagnostic records.
lost: Timely restoration; acknowledgment is not recovery.
falsifier: Acknowledgment triggers verified repair within the relevant deadline rather than merely a queue entry.
evidence: Qualitative conditional hypothesis from assigned scenarios; not observed in Factory.

name: Legitimate authority conflict
conditions: Two valid representatives issue incompatible decisions and an effective gate refuses to guess a precedence.
feedback: No restoring force; unresolved authority semantics sustain the hold.
entry: Concurrent approval/revocation or incompatible mandates with no established ordering.
exit: A competent authority resolves scope and precedence, or the operation is abandoned.
survives: Conflicting instructions and ability to abstain at controlled boundaries.
lost: A uniquely legitimate action; immediate throughput.
falsifier: A pre-existing valid rule uniquely orders the decisions for this operation, or participants already acted on both.
evidence: Qualitative conditional hypothesis from assigned scenarios; not observed in Factory.

name: Oversight captured or inaccessible
conditions: The only alert/account authority is unavailable, departed, or conflicted and no independent authorized observer can change it.
feedback: Control holder can suppress evidence of its own conduct, preserving control; persistence still depends on account governance or the installed mute policy.
entry: Sole monitoring account retained after departure, alarms silenced by interested team, or legitimate successor locked out.
exit: Independent lawful account recovery or governance changes restore effective oversight; missing history may remain lost.
survives: Business actions may continue and the account may still function for its controller.
lost: Independent visibility and legitimate intervention path.
falsifier: An independent authorized party can inspect and act despite the alleged exclusive account control.
evidence: Qualitative conditional hypothesis from assigned scenarios; not observed in Factory.

name: Provider-bound service ended
kind: service loss relative to a boundary
conditions: Required provider permanently stops and no presently usable compatible substitute exists.
feedback: None required. Supplier cessation is external; irrecoverability of all business function is not established.
entry: Shutdown deadline passes before usable migration or export.
exit: Alternative provider or local implementation becomes viable; otherwise retire the dependent function. Lost provider-only data may be unrecoverable.
survives: Locally interpretable records and independent services.
lost: That provider capability; possibly provider-only data and continuity.
falsifier: A compatible alternative with legitimate credentials actually executes the required operation in time.
evidence: Qualitative conditional hypothesis from assigned scenarios; not observed in Factory.

name: Delayed liabilities still arriving
conditions: Usage/effects are already committed but their cost or acceptance reports arrive later than local budgeting or shutdown decisions.
feedback: No intrinsic loop. Repeated spending against understated cost can create recurrence only with a continuing policy and demand.
entry: Delayed billing, delayed acceptance, or obligations outliving local operation.
exit: All bounded pending liabilities settle with evidence; unknown/unbounded queues prevent demonstrated closure.
survives: Known accounting entries and possibly local spending stop.
lost: Reliable current budget headroom and a proven final liability amount.
falsifier: A hard provider-enforced ceiling bounds total committed cost, including unreported usage, and no hidden obligations remain.
evidence: Qualitative conditional hypothesis from assigned scenarios; not observed in Factory.

name: Speculation or retry overload
conditions: Response delay causes more copies/retries, which increase load and delay; control does not damp the loop.
feedback: Latency -> extra requests -> congestion/cost -> more latency. Warm and overloaded basins may coexist under the same base demand.
entry: Aggressive tail target or cold restore cache with outstanding operations; retry amplification exceeds spare capacity.
exit: Effective admitted work falls below capacity long enough to drain and warm; old accepted copies still require outcome accounting.
survives: Some successful requests and local journals if not exhausted.
lost: Predictable latency, cost and perhaps unique external effects if deduplication is absent.
falsifier: Duplicate work is coalesced or capped so the burst drains under unchanged base demand; no self-sustaining overload occurs.
evidence: Qualitative conditional hypothesis from assigned scenarios; not observed in Factory.

name: Legally or safely withheld operation
conditions: A competent applicable prohibition or safety boundary is known and the last effective boundary actually refuses the action.
feedback: No feedback needed. Policy enforcement holds the operation; this is not proof the physical world is safe.
entry: Prohibition, unsafe context, or expired mandate is detected before acceptance.
exit: Legitimate resolution and fresh safety assessment permit new work, or the action is abandoned. Contradictory legal duties may remain unresolved.
survives: Evidence of refusal and prevention at the boundaries that enforce it.
lost: Requested action throughput; already buffered actions may escape this hold.
falsifier: A participant accepts under the old authorization despite the stated prohibition or safety boundary.
evidence: Qualitative conditional hypothesis from assigned scenarios; not observed in Factory.

name: Schedule meaning or expiry drift
conditions: A stored clock/calendar interpretation no longer matches intended elapsed time or civil-time meaning, and policy keeps using it.
feedback: No autonomous attraction. A backwards clock may retain a mute; changed time rules may repeatedly mis-time scheduled work.
entry: Suspend semantics, wall-clock jump, time-zone reform, or deferral beyond validity.
exit: Intent is re-established with current trustworthy timing evidence; ambiguity may instead require BD02.
survives: Stored times and perhaps local monotone order within valid clock epochs.
lost: Correct relation to elapsed time or intended local appointment; not necessarily every schedule.
falsifier: The stored semantics explicitly distinguish fixed instant from civil recurrence and detect epoch discontinuities correctly.
evidence: Qualitative conditional hypothesis from assigned scenarios; not observed in Factory.

name: Contradictory evidence retained
conditions: Different observations disagree about identity, liveness, historical order or effect and no trusted discriminator is available.
feedback: No inherent loop. A policy not to collapse disagreement preserves an unresolved assessment.
entry: Conflicting journals, runtime/file/agent claims, or recipient/provider testimony.
exit: Independent provenance, causal ordering or direct effect evidence resolves the relevant question; signatures alone may not.
survives: Multiple claims and their provenance if preserved.
lost: A uniquely justified history or outcome.
falsifier: Disagreement is explained by different time intervals/subjects, or independent causal evidence selects a consistent interpretation.
evidence: Source distinguishes confidence and leaves idle/done task signals unchanged; it does not arbitrate arbitrary competing business evidence.

name: Rewarded metric substitution
conditions: Agents or teams are rewarded for a proxy and can exclude difficult cases, relabel incidents or report unverified artifacts without external outcome checks.
feedback: Proxy improvement -> reward/trust -> greater selection/reporting latitude -> more proxy improvement while real quality worsens. Can persist after one misleading report.
entry: Measured denominator, classification, or artifact status is controlled by the evaluated actor.
exit: Independent outcome and rejected-work accounting changes the payoff, or the actor loses control over the proxy.
survives: Attractive metrics, finished-looking artifacts and perhaps easy-case throughput.
lost: Reliable meaning of success, availability and throughput.
falsifier: Rejected work and relabelled downtime remain counted, or rewards fall when independently checked quality falls.
evidence: Qualitative conditional hypothesis from assigned scenarios; not observed in Factory.

name: Planned shutdown mistaken for recurring failure
conditions: An energy schedule turns the host off and monitoring treats each planned absence as an unexpected total failure.
feedback: External daily schedule drives recurrence; no autonomous failure oscillation established.
entry: Off-hours power policy and alert expectations disagree.
exit: Power schedule or monitoring interpretation changes; essential obligations must still be assessed independently.
survives: Daytime operation and possibly persisted tasks.
lost: Nighttime service and alert credibility; hazards depend on required nighttime work.
falsifier: Outages continue with the schedule disabled, or off-hours monitoring already distinguishes expected absence.
evidence: Qualitative conditional hypothesis from assigned scenarios; not observed in Factory.

name: Archive bytes without a trustworthy interpreter
conditions: An artifact survives but available CPU/format/software cannot reliably recover its intended semantics.
feedback: No intrinsic loop. Missing interpreter or specification sustains inability to use the archive.
entry: Native representation restored across architectures or obsolete format dependencies disappear.
exit: A validated interpreter or independent semantic reconstruction becomes available; total loss is not assumed merely from obsolescence.
survives: Raw bytes and any external specification or human-readable context.
lost: Current trustworthy execution or interpretation.
falsifier: A portable encoding and independent decoder reproduce the intended semantics, not just a plausible value.
evidence: Qualitative conditional hypothesis from assigned scenarios; not observed in Factory.

name: Distinct names collapsed with information lost
conditions: Restore maps formerly distinct paths to one identity and overwrites unique content; no surviving separate copy contains it.
feedback: None. Aliasing alone is a detectable conflict; absorption requires actual unrecoverable overwrite.
entry: Case-sensitive source meets case-insensitive destination and colliding writes are accepted.
exit: No exact reconstruction without another copy or semantic source; before overwrite the conflict can instead be held.
survives: One surviving namespace entry and unaffected workspaces.
lost: Unique overwritten content and distinction between its owners.
falsifier: Restore rejects collisions or preserves both contents under distinct identities.
evidence: Source provides runtime device/inode alias checks and explicitly denies durable/security identity. Cross-filesystem restore overwrite is hypothetical, not observed.

name: Local shutdown with outstanding external obligations
conditions: Factory or its monitoring contract has ended while a participant may still accept queued work or report liabilities.
feedback: No feedback needed. External retained work outlives local supervision; new forcing is not required for a delayed effect.
entry: Decommission or contract expiry precedes verifiable queue drain, rejection, or last export.
exit: Every relevant participant supplies reliable closure evidence, or later effects settle; silence alone is not closure.
survives: Any retained records and reachable legitimate recipient; participant queue may survive the host.
lost: Ability to assert that shutdown ended effects or observations.
falsifier: Participants provably discard pending work and reject the retired authority before supervision ends.
evidence: Qualitative conditional hypothesis from assigned scenarios; not observed in Factory.

name: All recovery information and legitimate actors gone
conditions: The scenario literally removes computer, monitor, communications, every backup and every legitimate recipient, with no surviving alternate source or authority.
feedback: None. There is no remaining system to form an attractor.
entry: Simultaneous complete loss of the stated recovery boundary.
exit: No endogenous recovery. Discovery of surviving information/authority changes the premise; a new system is not recovery of lost facts.
survives: Nothing inside the stated boundary; the outside world is not thereby assumed destroyed.
lost: Recoverable state and legitimate continuation inside this boundary.
falsifier: A surviving authorized person, independent copy, or external record can reconstruct relevant facts.
evidence: Qualitative conditional hypothesis from assigned scenarios; not observed in Factory.

name: Perfectly consistent observations cannot ground truth
conditions: Every accessible trusted observation has identical output in a true world and a false world, and no independent channel is permitted.
feedback: No dynamics inferred. Indistinguishability is an information limit, not an attractor or proof of system stability.
entry: All trusted sources share a consistent false foundation, or a hostile substrate supplies perfect internal reports.
exit: Access an independent discriminating fact; under the literal closed premise there is no observational exit.
survives: Internal consistency and ability to compute on supplied observations.
lost: Justified determination of which real world holds.
falsifier: Any accessible observation differs between the alleged worlds; ordinary independent physical checks break the premise.
evidence: Qualitative conditional hypothesis from assigned scenarios; not observed in Factory.

name: Trusted malicious substrate maintains its own credibility
conditions: Installed signed code controls health, history and verification and can retain its authority because those same reports justify continued trust.
feedback: Forged success -> no intervention or renewed trust -> continued malicious execution -> more forged success. Can persist after the update distributor disconnects.
entry: A signed malicious update crosses a trust boundary with enough authority to falsify local evidence and remove competing history.
exit: An independently trusted observer or execution boundary exposes and excludes the code; erased unique history may remain unrecoverable.
survives: Apparent operation and whatever data lie outside malicious control.
lost: Integrity of internal evidence and possibly confidentiality/history; extent is not knowable from forged reports alone.
falsifier: Independent attestation or out-of-band evidence detects divergence, or the installed code cannot control every claimed check.
evidence: Qualitative conditional hypothesis from assigned scenarios; not observed in Factory.

name: Business continues outside monitor visibility
conditions: Factory can reach business participants but monitor-to-Factory observation is broken; no effective participant fence stops work.
feedback: No internal feedback required; network topology sustains asymmetric knowledge. Automated failover may add BD08.
entry: One-way or selective network partition separates liveness observer from active business paths.
exit: Observation path heals or an effective participant authority change stops old work; starting another clone alone is not resolution.
survives: Original business execution and local records.
lost: Monitor knowledge of execution and confidence that failover is exclusive.
falsifier: Actual business paths are also blocked, or participants reject all old work when monitoring loses contact.
evidence: Qualitative conditional hypothesis from assigned scenarios; not observed in Factory.

name: Necessary prerequisite unavailable
conditions: Repair or startup needs a toolchain, account or credential that is currently unavailable; no circular dependency or permanent impossibility is established.
feedback: None inherent. Unavailability maintains the wait; repeated costly workarounds can separately create BD13.
entry: A repair or emergency startup encounters a missing prerequisite that ordinary running work may not need.
exit: A legitimate compatible substitute or restored prerequisite becomes available; permanent cessation without substitute can instead yield BD22.
survives: Existing binaries, readable records and functions not needing the missing prerequisite.
lost: Immediate ability to repair or start affected functions.
falsifier: The operation completes using an independently available compatible prerequisite.
evidence: Qualitative conditional hypothesis from assigned scenarios; not observed in Factory.
